# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy to New Billing System

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 existing users from the old billing system to the new one in three named phases, run while both systems operate concurrently (dual-run). Migration is a one-way move of a user's billing record and active state from old → new; the old system remains live, receiving no new migrations, until a separate, later decommissioning effort begins — which is explicitly out of scope for this rollout and must not start during the final migration phase.

---

## Phase 1: Canary

**Population:** 1% of users (~400 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full parity testing in staging (100% of test suite including tax, proration, refund, and dunning scenarios), reconciliation tooling between old and new systems is deployed and verified against a synthetic dataset, and a rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end in staging.

**Selection:** Internal/employee accounts and a small set of consenting low-risk external users (no active disputes, no enterprise contracts, simple monthly plans only). No high-value or annual-contract accounts included.

**Duration:** Minimum 5 business days, long enough to observe at least one full billing cycle event (invoice generation) for the cohort.

**Exit criterion to proceed to Phase 2:** Zero critical billing discrepancies (see metrics below), all Phase 1 users successfully invoiced at least once on the new system with amounts matching old-system shadow calculations within $0.01, and support ticket volume for the cohort is not statistically elevated versus baseline.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion

**Population:** 20% of users (~8,000 users, cumulative ~8,400 including Phase 1)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 exit criteria met and signed off by both Engineering and Finance leads; no unresolved Sev1/Sev2 incidents from Phase 1 remain open.

**Selection:** Broader mix of plan types (monthly, annual, usage-based) and geographies, but still excluding largest enterprise accounts (top 5% by revenue) and any accounts flagged for active payment disputes.

**Duration:** Minimum 10 business days, covering at least two billing cycle events including at least one annual-renewal event if annual plans are included.

**Exit criterion to proceed to Phase 3:** Reconciliation mismatch rate stays under threshold (see metrics), payment failure/decline rate for migrated cohort is within 0.5 percentage points of the old-system baseline, and no rollback was triggered during the phase.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (Full Migration)

**Population:** Remaining ~79% of users (~31,600 users), migrated in weekly sub-batches (e.g., 4–6 batches of ~5,000–8,000) rather than a single cutover, including highest-value and enterprise accounts last within this phase.

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 exit criteria met, dedicated support staffing and escalation runbook confirmed in place for the full migration window, and a finance close cycle has been completed cleanly (no material reconciliation issues) since Phase 2 began.

**Exit criterion (end of rollout):** 100% of the 40,000 users are on the new billing system, all metrics remain within threshold for two consecutive full billing cycles post-migration for the final batch, and Finance has signed off on end-to-end reconciliation for the entire user base.

**Note on decommissioning:** The old billing system is kept fully running, unmodified and available in read-only/reconciliation mode, throughout Phase 3, including the final batch. Any work to disable, delete, or decommission the old system must be scoped as a **separate, subsequent phase** that only begins after Phase 3's exit criteria are met and a defined post-migration observation window (minimum 30 days) has passed with no reopened billing discrepancies.

---

## Metrics and Automatic Halt Criteria

Rollout is automatically paused (no further users migrated into the current or next phase) if, at any point:

- **Reconciliation mismatch rate exceeds 0.1%** of migrated users' invoices in any 24-hour window (i.e., more than 1 in 1,000 migrated invoices shows a discrepancy vs. shadow calculation on the old system).
- **Payment failure rate for migrated users rises more than 2 percentage points** above the pre-migration baseline failure rate for the same cohort, measured over a rolling 48-hour window.
- **Critical/Sev1 incident count related to billing exceeds 2 in any 7-day period** for the migrated cohort.

When a halt is triggered, migration of new users stops, the on-call and Finance leads are paged, and no phase progression occurs until root cause is identified and a fix is verified in staging.

---

## Risks

RISK: Duplicate or double-billing of a user during the dual-run window if both systems attempt to invoice the same account | Implement a hard mutual-exclusion flag per user ID that marks which system is authoritative for billing, checked by both systems before invoice generation | Billing Platform Engineering Lead
RISK: Data drift between old and new systems for a migrated user due to a missed webhook or sync failure, causing incorrect balances | Run continuous automated reconciliation jobs comparing balances every 4 hours for all migrated users, with alerting on any mismatch | Data Reconciliation Team Lead
RISK: Payment processor or tax-calculation integration behaves differently under the new system, causing silent miscalculation at scale before detection | Shadow-mode run new-system calculations against 100% of old-system traffic for 2 weeks before Phase 1 begins, comparing outputs without acting on them | Finance Systems Engineering Lead
RISK: Support team is overwhelmed by migration-related tickets during Phase 3 due to volume, delaying detection of real billing issues | Stagger Phase 3 into weekly sub-batches sized to support team capacity, and stand up a dedicated migration support queue with defined SLAs | Customer Support Operations Manager
RISK: Rollback of a migrated user back to the old system is attempted but the old system's record is stale or missing recent activity, causing data loss | Freeze (read-only) a user's old-system record only after new-system invoicing is confirmed successful for one full cycle, never at the moment of migration | Billing Platform Engineering Lead

PHASES: 3
